description: Release/drift-tooling registry for profile ids that are not part of the current v1 profile matrix. Current ServiceDescribe claims, conformance reports and implementation manifests consume conformance-profiles.json; conformance scanners may consume this file for negative drift tests and release audit. This is CI/release drift-detection tooling, not a current-wire normative contract: every entry is hard-reject on the wire, there is no migration/compat tolerance window and no offline migration layer; removed ids MAY appear only in changelog documentation and in cotest negative drift fixtures that assert rejection.

rejection_levels.hard_reject: MUST be rejected if declared by a current implementation.
rejection_levels.docs_only: Removed from machine surfaces; survives in CHANGELOG / migration notes.

allowed_context_definitions.changelog: Reference in CHANGELOG or migration documentation.
allowed_context_definitions.negative_test: Reference in cotest drift fixtures that assert rejection.

entries.notes: Single-modality profile ids never existed as canonical ck.profile.* entries. Use ck.profile.chat_mvp.v1 + the Realm's actual schema declaration to describe a chat-focused product.
See chat_only_client. Use ck.profile.kanban_mvp.v1; modality is expressed via Realm schema / morph_type_profiles, not via single-modality profile gating.

Agent workspace profile was withdrawn from v1. Private agent context (mirror Realm + agent_task FSM + mention_redirect / import_attestation) is now treated as a deployment-local concern outside the canonical protocol. Generic agent participation is still supported via ck.member.state + ck.capability.grant + ck.agent.* protocol session events (ck.profile.agent_runtime.v1).
Reserved placeholder id removed with ck.profile.agent_workspace.v1.
Realm/Space inversion cleanup. Current v1 uses ck.profile.mls.minimal_metadata_realm.v1 because the profile scope is the Realm E2EE / routing boundary.

Removed from v1 governance. Realm/Circle moderation reports route to scoped administrators with reporter-supplied encrypted evidence and optional franking proof; they MUST NOT depend on exporter-secret verifiers or sender-bound plaintext commitment.
